title: Turkey Fajita Fried Rice Bowls
description: Vegetable fried rice topped with smoky spiced lean ground turkey, fresh tomato, Monterey Jack, and a Greek yogurt and lime finish
ingredients: 1 tbsp canola oil or extra virgin olive oil
1 lime, juiced (or 2 tbsp bottled lime juice)
instructions: In a small bowl, combine the spice blend: 1 tsp chili powder, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp onion powder, 1/2 tsp crushed red pepper flakes, 1/2 tsp dried oregano, 2 tsp paprika, 1 1/2 tsp ground cumin, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1 pinch cinnamon, and 1 pinch ground cloves. Set aside.

Bring 2 1/2 cups water and 1/4 tsp salt to a boil in a medium pot. Add 1 1/2 cups basmati rice, reduce heat to low, cover, and cook 12-14 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and keep covered.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Add 500g lean ground turkey, breaking it apart, and cook until fully browned and the internal temperature reaches 74°C/165°F.

Add 1/4 cup water, 3/4 tsp garlic salt, and the full spice blend from step 1 to the turkey. Stir to coat and simmer 2-3 minutes, until the water has mostly evaporated and the spices have bloomed and lost any raw, dusty taste.
Transfer the seasoned turkey to a bowl and set aside. Do not wipe out the pan.

Return the pan to medium-high heat. Add 320g sliced bell pepper, 1 diced medium zucchini (about 200g), 113g diced yellow onion, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, and 1 pinch salt. Cook 4-5 minutes until softened with some browning.
Stir in 2 chopped green onions and cook 1 minute. Add the cooked rice from step 2 and stir-fry over medium-high heat for 1-2 minutes to combine and pick up the spice residue from the pan.

Divide the vegetable fried rice among 4 bowls. Top each bowl with one quarter of the seasoned turkey, about 40g diced Roma tomato (160g total), and 1/4 cup shredded Monterey Jack cheese (1 cup / 113g total).

Finish each bowl with 1 1/2 tbsp 0% Greek yogurt (6 tbsp total) and about 1/2 tbsp lime juice (juice of 1 lime or 2 tbsp bottled lime juice total). Add black pepper to taste. Taste before adding any extra salt, because the lime makes the bowl taste saltier than it is.
notes: Protein density: about 6.6g protein per 100 kcal. Sodium is roughly 750mg per serving. Without cheese: about 533 cal, 35g protein, 68g carbs, 14g fat per serving, with protein density holding at about 6.6g per 100 kcal and sodium dropping to roughly 590mg. The 2-3 minute simmer in step 4 matters: it cooks out the raw edge of the cumin and paprika so the smaller amount of spice still tastes full. For more heat, increase the red pepper flakes rather than adding more of the full blend.
